title: These Bullets Won't Make It To Broadway

contact_edits.before: Now for the good stuff. Some of the attitudes, under Ron Jenkins' direction, are very impressive. Marie Nychka, the choreographer, has staged a wild ball. Much of the singing is muggy, but Michael Scholar Jr., as the diabolic tempter named Peg Leg, cuts through the haze with a ringing solo that warms up the theatre while chilling the blood. Rachael Johnston is marvellous as the heroine, especially when sharing a duet with her intended, he hiding under her skirts, she -- we have to assume -- standing on his shoulders. (This makes hers a literally towering performance.) Finally, within sight of the end, there's a slow-motion death-fall, hilarious and horrific at once, that comes as close as anything I've seen to making manifest the inexorable. It should invade the dreams of everyone who sees it. - The Black Rider runs until Nov. 16. Call 416-531-1827 for ticket and information.
